chat.initialMessage: Hello! I am your AI assistant MakeKeeper. Ready to help with pinouts, component selection, or code for your project. What's on your mind?
chat.esp32Response: To connect ESP32, remember: most GPIO pins operate at 3.3V logic level. Default I2C pins: SDA (GPIO 21), SCL (GPIO 22).
chat.transistorResponse: When choosing an n-channel field-effect transistor (MOSFET) for 3.3V/5V microcontroller control, look for "Logic-Level" models (e.g. IRLZ44N). Their gate threshold voltage Vgs(th) is significantly lower.
chat.defaultResponse: Great question! To give a precise answer, I might need the context of your active project. You can select it in the "Projects" tab.

list_ai_providers.description: Returns the list of configured AI providers WITHOUT secret keys: name, provider type, model, and the default-provider flag. Use it to find out which models are available.

resolve_object_ref.description: Resolves a canonical object reference (ORef, "mk://<plugin>/<type>/<id>") to the object's human name and breadcrumb path. Pass a reference you received from the page context or another tool's "ref" field to learn exactly what and where it is.

params.ref: The canonical ORef to resolve, e.g. "mk://storages/storage/<id>#B1".

read_attachment.description: Reads an attached file as text: a log, gcode, a config, a sketch, CSV or JSON. Pass the file reference you received in the message context or from list_project_files. A long file comes back in parts — repeat the call with "offset" set to the returned "nextOffset". A picture or a binary file returns no content, only its name, type and size.

params.ref: File reference ("mk://projects/file/<id>") or its raw id.
params.offset: Byte offset to read from. Omit for the beginning of the file.

read_attachment.notText: The file is not text and cannot be read.
read_attachment.isImage: This is a picture: it is already visible in the conversation and is not read as text.

prompt.systemIntro: You are a professional AI copilot and electronics assistant for MakeKeeper.
prompt.projectScope: You are working in the project “{title}” ({ref}). Fetch its tasks, parts and orders with the tools when the question needs them — they are not repeated here.
prompt.closingInstructions: Answer concisely and professionally. You have tools for working with the warehouse and the database. If you need data about the warehouse, box structure, or parts, call the appropriate tools.
prompt.photoRecognition:
### Component recognition from a photo
If the user has sent a photo of an electronic component and asks to identify it:
- Read the markings literally, character by character; do not guess or "correct" poorly legible characters.
- If the marking or part of it is illegible, write "unreadable" for that field directly instead of picking a plausible part number.
- Clearly separate what is actually visible in the photo from what you infer by guesswork; for guesses, indicate low confidence.
- Present the result by fields: Part number, Package, Manufacturer, Type/purpose, Confidence (high/medium/low). Mark fields that cannot be determined as "not determined".
prompt.pageContextRefs: - Selected object references (pass these to tools verbatim): {refs}
prompt.objectRefs:
### Object references (ORef)
Objects are identified by canonical references shaped like "mk://<plugin>/<type>/<id>" (with an optional "#<fragment>", e.g. a grid cell "#B1"). You receive them in the page context and in the "ref" field of tool results. Pass a reference back to a tool verbatim instead of a bare id; call resolve_object_ref to turn one into a human name and location.
When you mention an object in a reply, make the object's own NAME the clickable link: write it as a Markdown link whose visible text is the name and whose target is the ORef — for example `[LED Strip](mk://inventory/component/comp_f412tyy)`, which renders as just "LED Strip". NEVER print the raw "mk://…" string on its own or in parentheses after the name — the reader should see a normal-looking name, not the reference.

prompt.pageContextIntro: The user sent the message while on this screen. Take this into account when interpreting deictic expressions ("this project", "this part", "here", "show its tasks"). The context only clarifies intent and does NOT override the mandatory confirmation of dangerous (DESTRUCTIVE) actions.

gemini.title: How to get a Google Gemini API key:
steps: Open Google AI Studio → API keys (the direct API-keys page).
Sign in with your Google account — a personal Gmail account works.
Click "Create API key", then choose or create a Google Cloud project when asked.
Copy the key that appears and paste it into the "Personal API Key" field above.
Leave the base URL at its default unless you use a proxy. The free tier is enough to get started — no billing card required.

openai.title: How to get an OpenAI API key:
steps: Open the OpenAI Platform → API keys page.
Sign up or log in, and verify your email and phone number if prompted.
Open Billing and add a payment method, then top up credits — OpenAI keys don't work until billing is enabled.
Click "Create new secret key", give it a name, and confirm.
Copy the key immediately — it is shown only once — and paste it above. The optional Organization ID (starts with "org-") is under Settings → Organization if you belong to several organizations.

anthropic.title: How to get an Anthropic (Claude) API key:
steps: Open the Anthropic Console → API keys page.
Sign up or log in and verify your email address.
Open Plans & Billing and buy credits — a new key needs credits before it will work.
Click "Create Key", name it, and copy the value (it is shown only once).
Paste the key above. Leave "API Version" at 2023-06-01 unless Anthropic's documentation tells you to change it.

ollama.title: How to connect a local Ollama server:
steps: Download and install Ollama for your operating system from ollama.com/download.
Start the Ollama application (or run "ollama serve"). It listens on http://localhost:11434 by default.
In a terminal, download a model with "ollama pull llama3.1" (replace with any model you want to use).
Enter the server address in the base URL field and the model name (e.g. llama3.1) in the model field. No API key is required.

custom.title: How to connect a custom gateway or proxy:
steps: Use this option for a self-hosted proxy or any OpenAI/Gemini/Anthropic-compatible gateway (for example LiteLLM or OpenRouter).
Enter your gateway's full base URL, including any "/v1" path, in the base URL field.
If your gateway requires an access token, paste it into the API key field; otherwise leave it empty.
Set the model field to a model id your gateway exposes. Check your gateway's documentation for the exact endpoint and model names.
